title: The full test run never fails on a speed budget that passes alone
goal: A handful of speed tests fail when the whole suite runs and pass every time on their own, so a green release has needed a second full run (about two minutes each) and every session has to stop and prove the failure was load, not a regression. A speed test should catch a real slowdown without failing just because the rest of the suite is running beside it.
notes: User asked for this 2026-10-29 after the v0.21.0 release. History: release v0.20.0 (2026-10-27) first run missed the brush grid (3.3 s) and the animated chart (37.4 vs 36.8 ms), rerun green; the timeline-room worktree's commits noted the same kind of misses (AnimatedChartRender + CaptionCost, then WebPEncodeSpeed, then the brush grid at 3.5 s); release v0.21.0 first run missed the brush grid (3.7 s) and the chart (64.0 vs 54.8 ms), rerun green. Each passed alone in a fraction of its limit (brush suite 2.6 s, chart suite 1.4 s). Tests live in Tests/PhotonzRenderTests (BrushPreviewTests.swift around line 149, AnimatedChartRenderTests.swift line 153, CaptionCostTests.swift, WebPEncodeSpeedTests.swift). Scripts/test.sh splits the suite into four parallel runs using Scripts/test-weights.tsv and a .serialized group; read CLAUDE.md's test section before changing how it splits. Do not lift SWT_EXPERIMENTAL_MAXIMUM_PARALLELIZATION_WIDTH.
acceptance: Measured first: run Scripts/test.sh in full at least five times and record, for each speed test that ever misses, how often and by how much, in the audit. Known repeat offenders: BrushPreviewTests theWholeGridPaintsWithoutAStall (a fixed 3000 ms limit on the slowest tile; missed at 3.3, 3.5 and 3.7 s), AnimatedChartRenderTests 'Every chart at 1080p draws inside a frame while it builds' (MachineSpeed.budget 10.5 ms baseline; missed at 37.4 vs 36.8 and 64.0 vs 54.8 ms), and also seen once each: CaptionCostTests and WebPEncodeSpeedTests.

Fix the cause, not the number alone: either such a test runs where nothing else competes for the cores (its own run in Scripts/test.sh, like the .serialized group), or its limit is judged against a yardstick measured under the same load at the same moment (as MachineSpeed does for other budgets), or both. A fixed millisecond limit with no yardstick (the brush grid's 3000) goes.
Each test still catches a real regression: show, in the audit, that making the measured code 2x slower fails the test in the full run (put the slowdown in on a scratch branch, never committed).
Ten full Scripts/test.sh runs in a row with no speed-budget failure, on this Mac with the go loop idle, recorded in the audit. The whole run takes no longer than today's 123 to 128 s.
CI's three slices also stay green on them (check the last few Release and CI runs for these names).
Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not.
